scope: Official major Go 1.18 through 1.27 notes, captured 2026-10-11; supplemental patch status remains separate.

counts.atomic_change_count: not claimed; groups may cover related APIs and qualifications

method: Read full B source text, including nonrecords, and author detailed section-level paraphrases. Align all A/C evidence by normalized full text or reviewed containment. Reconcile their semantic domain lenses to these narrower groups. Review all unmatched source units individually. Retain every meaningful API, behavior, platform/tooling change and qualification rather than first-sentence summaries.

items.section: Changes to the language / Generics
items.summary: Type parameters support generic functions and types, instantiated with bracketed type arguments. Interfaces can express type sets using unions and ~ underlying types, but these generalized interfaces are constraints, not ordinary value types. any aliases interface{} and comparable constrains equality-capable types. The initial implementation lacks production experience and specification or compiler corrections can invalidate buggy code. The x/exp helpers have no Go 1 compatibility promise.
items.implication_applicability: Generic syntax and constraint interfaces require Go 1.18 language support. Production-readiness warnings describe the initial compiler, while x/exp stability depends on that external module rather than the standard-library compatibility promise.

items.section: Changes to the language / Experimental maps and initial generic implementation restrictions
items.summary: Experimental x/exp/maps supplies generic map operations. Separately, the initial generics implementation disallows local type declarations in generic functions, real/imag/complex on type parameters, implicit constraint methods, common struct-field access, embedding type parameters or their pointers, and multi-term unions containing method-bearing interfaces. Tools and libraries need generics support. Promised possible relaxations are not implemented features.
items.implication_applicability: The map helpers are experimental external-module APIs. The listed restrictions describe the initial Go 1.18 generic compiler and language implementation, not additional map-package restrictions. Check later releases before treating a historical restriction as current.

items.section: Changes to the language / Bug fixes
items.summary: The compiler rejects variables only assigned inside closures but never used, and rejects overflowing rune constants passed to print/println. Repair invalid code or explicitly select the intended type. Compatibility does not preserve these compiler bugs.
items.implication_applicability: These are corrected diagnostics in the Go 1.18 compiler. The release notes provide no older-module-language escape hatch. Repair the invalid code when adopting the corrected compiler.

items.section: Standard library / New net/netip package

items.section: Runtime
items.summary: GOMEMLIMIT/debug.SetMemoryLimit sets a soft limit on runtime-managed memory, excluding external allocations and OS-held memory. It works with GOGC, even GOGC=off. Very small limits may overshoot. To preserve progress near the live-heap size, GC limits its CPU use near 50% excluding idle time and may exceed the memory limit. The limiter metric exposes activation. Idle periodic GC uses fewer workers, initial stacks adapt to historical usage, and importing os raises Unix RLIMIT_NOFILE to the hard limit (potentially affecting old child programs). Fatal application errors show shorter tracebacks unless system/crash is requested. ARM64 supports debugger-injected calls and ASan tracks arguments/globals more precisely.

items.section: Changes to the language
items.summary: min/max operate on a fixed list of arguments. clear deletes map entries or zeroes slice elements. Package initialization chooses the first import-path-sorted package whose imports are initialized, so implicit ordering dependencies can change. Inference now handles generic function arguments/assignments/returns, matching interface and constraint methods, mixed untyped constants, and stricter component-type identity. Per-iteration loop variables are only a preview here. panic(nil) produces *runtime.PanicNilError so direct deferred recover during panic cannot return nil. panicnil=1 restores old behavior and defaults on for main modules declaring go 1.20 or earlier.
items.implication_applicability: Separate the Go 1.21 built-ins and inference changes from clarified initialization ordering, the opt-in loop-variable preview, and panic(nil) runtime compatibility. The panicnil default follows the main module version: go 1.20 or earlier retains the old behavior. A single language-feature gate does not describe all these changes.

items.section: Standard library / Minor changes to the library / crypto/tls
items.summary: Resumed TLS servers skip client-certificate re-verification and VerifyPeerCertificate except expiry checks. On session resumption, clients check expiry even with InsecureSkipVerify. SessionState/Bytes/ParseSessionState, WrapSession/UnwrapSession, EncryptTicket/DecryptTicket and client ResumptionState APIs expose ticket management. Servers rotate tickets on every resumption and remove key identifiers, reducing tracking but increasing trial-key cost. Extended Master Secret restores TLSUnique for supported resumed sessions. QUICConn supports QUIC handshakes and 0-RTT but is not a QUIC transport and does not add TLS 0-RTT. VersionName formats versions. For TLS 1.3 connections requiring client authentication through RequireAnyClientCert or RequireAndVerifyClientCert, a missing client certificate produces the certificate-required alert. An untrusted issuing CA produces the unknown-certificate-authority alert. Expired or not-yet-valid certificates produce the expired-certificate alert. Other client-authentication failures retain bad-certificate.

items.section: Runtime / Container-aware GOMAXPROCS
items.summary: On Linux, default GOMAXPROCS considers cgroup CPU bandwidth limits, not Kubernetes CPU requests. On all platforms, the runtime can periodically refresh defaults when available CPUs change, also considering changed cgroup limits on Linux. On Go 1.25+ these behaviors default on for program compatibility defaults >=1.25. For defaults <=1.24, containermaxprocs and updatemaxprocs both default to 0. Program defaults follow the active workspace or work module, with godebug and main-package //go:debug overrides. Per-file language gates do not select them. Runtime GODEBUG environment settings can override these defaults. Explicit positive GOMAXPROCS environment settings or runtime.GOMAXPROCS calls that set a value override automatic selection and disable updates. The two GODEBUG settings independently control the behaviors. Cgroup file descriptors remain cached.
items.implication_applicability: Check the toolchain, program defaults with go list -f '{{.DefaultGODEBUG}}' for the actual main package, and runtime GODEBUG overrides before relying on quota awareness or automatic updates. Linux quota awareness and updates on all platforms are distinct. Exact default selection also considers CPU affinity; consult runtime documentation for quota rounding and the minimum rule.

items.section: Standard library / New encoding/json/v2 and encoding/json/jsontext packages
items.summary: JSONv2/jsontext become supported. v2 Marshal/MarshalWrite/MarshalEncode and Unmarshal/UnmarshalRead/UnmarshalDecode accept Options, defaulting to rejection of invalid UTF-8 and duplicate object names. jsontext Encoder/Decoder process Token/Value streams with syntax-state validation. Legacy encoding/json uses the engine while preserving v1 semantics except error wording and remains supported. nojsonv2 temporarily restores the original engine. Experimental migration removes format/unknown tags, DiscardUnknownMembers and SkipFunc; inline becomes embed; string tags and MatchCaseInsensitiveNames change; numeric Token accessors now return errors. Encoding remains broadly comparable in speed while decoding improves.

book_update_matrix.book_update: Rewrite the old blanket loop-variable capture warning for Go 1.22+ semantics. Variables declared by the loop are per iteration, while externally shared variables remain shared. Also review no-copy values in three-clause loops.

Version-gate the old requirements to stop unreachable timers and drain stale timer values. Go 1.23 changes collection and channels under module-version controls. Go 1.27 removes the asynchronous-channel opt-out.
A comparable type argument does not prove every dynamic interface value is safe to compare. Keep the possible runtime panic in generic map/equality guidance.
Explain GOMEMLIMIT as a soft limit on Go-managed memory. Leave room for unmanaged allocations and the runtime choosing progress over the limit.

Do not blindly set GOMAXPROCS to NumCPU. Go 1.25 adds Linux quota awareness and automatic updates on all platforms. Program compatibility defaults <=1.24 set containermaxprocs/updatemaxprocs to 0. Check the active workspace or work module, explicit compatibility overrides and runtime settings. Per-file language versions do not select these runtime defaults.

Prefer AddCleanup over SetFinalizer for new finalization code, while treating explicit resource ownership as primary. Cleanup work can be concurrent. Weak pointers are for specialized structures, not ordinary ownership.

Replace assumptions about a deterministic global math/rand stream. Automatic seeding arrives in Go 1.20; global Seed becomes a no-op by default in Go 1.24. Use a local generator for reproducible tests.
Recover no longer normally returns nil for panic(nil) from Go 1.21 defaults. Do not use the old ambiguity as a universal rule.
Use context cancellation causes when callers need the reason. Use WithoutCancel intentionally because it separates a derived context from cancellation.
WaitGroup.Go can replace routine Add/go/defer Done bookkeeping in Go 1.25+. Retain lifecycle rules and account for vet checks for misplaced Add.
B.Loop offers a safer benchmark structure from Go 1.24. Account for the Go 1.26 fix that permits inlining while preventing whole benchmark work from being optimized away.
Keep cancellation and completion protocols. Add the supported Go 1.27 goroutineleak profile as a diagnosis tool, and state that reachable blocking primitives can hide leaks from the detector.
Exact slice growth, heap layout, stack placement, and closure code pointers are not stable contracts. Compiler changes can expose pre-existing unsafe bugs.
From Go 1.27, methods may introduce type parameters. Interface methods still may not, and generic methods do not implement them. Update old no-generic-methods statements only with the version gate.

Go 1.27 makes JSON v2/jsontext available and runs v1 on the new engine. v2 rejects invalid UTF-8 and duplicate object names by default. Do not mechanically transfer experimental tag names: inline becomes embed and several options are removed.
Use os.Root when an operation must stay beneath a directory, including against symlink escapes. Match the specific operation to the available Go version.
Replace Director with Rewrite because a malicious client can designate added headers as hop-by-hop and remove them under the old API. This is a correctness/security change, not cosmetic renaming.
Continue closing response bodies and defining ownership. Go 1.27 performs bounded draining on HTTP/1 Close for reuse. Bounded draining is not a promise to consume arbitrary unread bodies.
Treat the module go version as a strict minimum from Go 1.21. Account for automatic toolchain selection when reproducing builds or deciding which language/library features are legal.

Remove obsolete recovery instructions for asynctimerchan, tlsunsafeekm, tlsrsakex, tls3des, tls10server, x509keypairleaf, and gotypesalias on Go 1.27. Removed settings in module/source declarations cannot be set to their old behavior.
Use current go fix and vet checks to support migrations, then review behavior and tests. Go 1.27 test defaults include stdversion, so newer APIs in an older declared language version are diagnosed.

Review hand-written collection/search/sort/split code against stable slices/maps/cmp and iterator helpers. Account for zeroed slice tails and aliasing, and use Clone only when independent storage is needed.
Update single-chain error assumptions for Join and multiple %w operands. errors.Is/As traverse children; AsType adds a typed extraction option in 1.26.
Add synctest with its stable 1.25 Test API, preserving the different 1.24 experiment. Fake time and bubble blocking do not replace race detection or all integration tests.
Extend testing guidance with testing.F, fuzz budgets/cache cleanup and application coverage using GOCOVERDIR.
Prefer clear typed atomic state where atomics are appropriate. Keep sequential consistency, alignment and lifecycle requirements separate from availability of TryLock or atomic bitwise operators.
Use explicit executable paths when current-directory execution is intended. Cmd.Cancel/WaitDelay improve cancellation and descendant-pipe handling without removing ownership responsibilities.
Consider slog and handler validation rather than unstructured-only examples. Respect key/value vet checks, handler composition and log sensitivity.
Refresh benchmark/profile advice for PGO, aggregate mutex delay, trace flight recording and evolving collectors. Do not preserve old percentages, heap layout or allocation assumptions as contracts.

Keep noncryptographic local generators distinct from secure randomness. New crypto APIs increasingly ignore custom readers; use scoped cryptotest support and preserve ECDSA nil deterministic signing. Track deprecated primitives and temporary compatibility switches.
Distinguish omitzero from omitempty, including zero time.Time. A pointer produced by new(expression) is available only with 1.26 language support.
Update ServeMux patterns, method behavior, path captures and 307 slash redirects. Preserve request/response resource bounds and configure CSRF protection for its specific browser threat model.

disagreements_and_corrections.resolution: All 1,285 A records and 1,335 C records reconcile to B evidence. C additionally extracts 29 package headings and one specification-link continuation. A combines two initialization-order list steps. C splits an integer-range paragraph/code example. No minority behavioral change was discarded.

Go 1.19 calls OmitHost an empty-authority marker imprecisely. Official parser/string implementation distinguishes absent authority (http:/path, OmitHost true) from explicit empty authority (http:///path).

Go 1.22 says Extended Master Secret was supported since 1.20, while Go 1.21 explicitly announces its implementation. Use the 1.21 introduction and the independently clear 1.22 EKM restriction, not the conflicting retrospective date.
The broad 1.26 ECDSA custom-randomness statement has a documented nil special case: PrivateKey.Sign(nil,...) remains deterministic RFC6979. Official source confirms the distinction.

Major notes include later security fixes. Preserve explicit 1.19.8/1.20.3 template gates. The 1.20 multipart paragraph repeats a 1.19.8 threshold, so do not infer that 1.20.0 had those limits from its placement.
The served 1.24 notes now include tlskyber removal; 1.27 also documents that earlier removal. Treat these as two source statements about one historical change, not two removals.

Earlier predictions do not prove later implementation. In particular, 1.18 bootstrap plans differ from actual 1.20 adoption, and 1.26 predicts nogreenteagc removal but 1.27 notes do not confirm it. No unconfirmed removal is asserted.

cross_release_cautions: Go 1.18's planned bootstrap increase did not establish Go 1.19's actual requirement. Go 1.20's notes explain the later adoption of Go 1.17.13.
Go 1.18's x/exp slices/maps/constraints are not the Go 1.21 standard-library packages. Keep origin and stability distinct.
Go 1.20 comparable satisfaction permits interface-containing types, but comparison can still panic. This is not a guarantee that all such runtime values are safely comparable.
Go 1.21's loop experiment is not Go 1.22's version-selected loop semantics. Three-clause loops also create fresh variables, which explains later copylock diagnostics.
Go 1.23's timer change is module-version-selected with an escape hatch. Go 1.27 removes the escape hatch and makes synchronous timer channels unconditional.
Go 1.24's testing/synctest Run API is experimental. Go 1.25's supported API uses Test. Do not carry experimental examples forward without checking their version.
Go 1.24's B.Loop prevented some inlining. Go 1.26 corrects that behavior while retaining protection against optimizing benchmark work away.
Go 1.25's JSON v2 is experimental. Go 1.27 publishes it after API removals/renames and uses it beneath v1, preserving v1 behavior except possible error-message text.
Go 1.25's Green Tea experiment becomes the Go 1.26 default. An earlier note predicting an opt-out removal does not itself prove removal in the next release.
Go 1.26's goroutine-leak profile becomes supported in Go 1.27, but reachability-based detection still misses some permanent blocking.
Go 1.27's limited automatic HTTP body draining weakens a blanket claim that every unread body must always be fully drained manually. Closing remains necessary and the drain is bounded.
TLS GODEBUG removals do not necessarily remove all explicit configuration support for older algorithms. Each removed switch's documented final behavior must be read separately.
Go 1.27 documents the earlier tlskyber removal, and the currently served Go 1.24 notes also include that removal. These are two source statements about one historical change.
Security fixes listed under earlier release notes can have explicit patch thresholds such as Go 1.19.8 and Go 1.20.3. Do not silently move them to the original major release.
Go 1.27 generic methods cannot implement interface methods. This is a material constraint on proposed design updates.

audit.structural_coverage_is_not_semantic_proo: Independent semantic review remains required; every full-text source unit can be checked against its linked paraphrase.

limits: This counts semantic section groups, not atomic APIs and not skill rules. Related details may share one canonical item.
Official major release notes define scope; unlisted commits and patch issues are not inferred.
Historical plans, experiments, temporary switches and module/patch gates remain historical facts rather than universal current recommendations.
Full scraped source stays in investigations/sources scratch files; this portable result contains paraphrases, mappings and official locators.
Current implementation was consulted narrowly for actual release-note wording conflicts; such supplemental sources are identified.
